definitions.explanation: A direction or position that is neither horizontal nor vertical.
Moving or positioned at an angle.

examples.japanese: {斜|なな}めに{線|せん}を{引|ひ}く。
{絵|え}が{斜|なな}めになっているので、{直|なお}してください。
examples.english: The picture is crooked, so please fix it.

examples.japanese: {交差点|こうさてん}を{斜|なな}めに{渡|わた}る。
{彼|かれ}の{家|いえ}は{駅|えき}の{斜|なな}め{向|む}かいにある。
examples.english: His house is diagonally across from the station.

notes:
{斜|なな}め functions as both a noun and a no-adjective (modifies nouns with の).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {斜|なな}めに (diagonally - adverbial)
- {斜|なな}め{前|まえ} (diagonally forward/ahead)
- {斜|なな}め{後|うし}ろ (diagonally behind)
- {斜|なな}め{向|む}かい (diagonally opposite)

DIRECTIONAL EXPRESSIONS:
- {斜|なな}め{右|みぎ} (diagonally to the right)
- {斜|なな}め{左|ひだり} (diagonally to the left)
- {斜|なな}め{上|うえ} (diagonally above)
- {斜|なな}め{下|した} (diagonally below)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {斜|なな}め vs. {傾|かたむ}いている: {傾|かたむ}いている means "tilted/leaning" (from vertical); {斜|なな}め describes diagonal direction.

RELATED KANJI:
{斜} is also read as しゃ in compounds like {傾斜|けいしゃ} (slope, inclination).

Register: Neutral. Common in everyday directions and descriptions.
